questions: Did the wider ±0.04 m span reduce off-track exits on s-bend and slalom compared with iteration 1 (1 of 20 and 0 of 20 finished)? Report off-track counts and max_error per track.

Did the 0.02 m spacing with a 0.012 m footprint leave dead zones between sensors (the gap at about ±0.01 m from centre), and did the signal stay monotonic? If not, would sensor_size 0.016 m be the better fix?
On the oval, did steering_oscillation (0.31 in iteration 1) fall after the weights were scaled? Is the oval finish rate (13 of 20 before) maintained?
Did the wider span push the signal into saturation on the sharpest bends, and if so, should the weights be reduced rather than the spacing changed?
feedback_request.suggested_changes_to_test: If s-bend and slalom still exit off-track with max_error above 0.05 m, try sensor_size 0.016 m with the same spacing to close the gaps between sensors. If oval steering_oscillation stays above 0.2 while max_error is low, reduce the weights to [-1,-0.5,0,0.5,1] before changing the geometry. Raise wheel_radius to 0.035 m only if a run completes with completion_time above about 3 s.

intent: Widen the five-sensor array from ±0.03 m to ±0.04 m at 0.02 m spacing, keeping the forward position y = 0.06 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_track 0.11 m, mass 0.7 kg and wheel_radius 0.03 m. The aim is to see the tape earlier on s-bend and slalom, where iteration 1 left max_error at 0.062 to 0.063 m with 1 to 1.3 line-loss events per run. The Integrator should keep the weight shape symmetric (for example [-2,-1,0,1,2] or a scaled version to suit the wider span). If the Integrator sees high steering_oscillation with low max_error, they may reduce the weights to [-1,-0.5,0,0.5,1] rather than adding geometry.
learning: Iteration 1 showed that oval finishes at 1.83 s, so speed is not the limit. The failures are concentrated on the tighter bends, which supports a wider span as the direct lever. Iteration 2 is designed to separate the effect of span from the controller's weight scaling, so the result should show whether oscillation is a weight problem or a geometry problem.
rationale: Iteration 1 raised the score from 48 to 337.5, with 13 of 20 oval runs finishing (mean 1.83 s, max_error 0.044). The s-bend and slalom tracks still fail: s-bend finished 1 of 20 (max_error 0.062, 1.3 line-loss events per run) and slalom finished 0 of 20 (max_error 0.063, 1.1 line-loss events). Every failure is an off-track exit with max_error at the 0.06 m floor, so the line is still being lost on sharper bends. The Integrator's rule applies: off-track exits persist with max_error above 0.05 m and line-loss events of at least 1, so I widen the sensor span to x = -0.04 to +0.04 m at 0.02 m spacing, as requested. The oval completion time (1.83 s) shows speed is not limiting, so wheel_radius stays at 0.03 m. The oval steering_oscillation of 0.31 is high while oval max_error is low (0.044), which matches the Integrator's weight-reduction condition. I am not changing the sensor layout for that. I am flagging it so the Integrator can decide whether to scale the weights, since the weights belong to the controller. I keep wheel_track 0.11, mass 0.7, sensor_size 0.012 and sensor y = 0.06, so the only geometry change is the wider span. Expected result: fewer off-track exits on s-bend and slalom, with max_error falling below about 0.05 m, while oval finishes at least as often as before.
